biography: Marcelo Zebra hails from the vibrant favelas of Rio de Janeiro, a world away from the polished circuits he now graces. His journey began not with go-karts but with navigating the chaotic streets on his battered bicycle, a skill that honed his reflexes and spatial awareness. Racing wasn't a dream initially; survival was. But when a local mechanic, noticing Marcelo's uncanny ability to predict traffic flow, introduced him to sim racing, a spark ignited. He quickly dominated local online leagues, earning enough prize money to fund his first karting season. The transition wasn't seamless – the raw physicality of real racing was a shock – but Marcelo's determination, fueled by the memory of his humble beginnings, saw him persevere. After a promising showing in Formula Brazil, he was picked up by F.Inter MG-15, a move that represents a crucial step in his ambition to reach the pinnacle of motorsport.
drivingStyle: Marcelo's driving style is characterized by calculated aggression. He possesses an uncanny ability to read track conditions and adapt his line accordingly. While he isn't afraid to push the limits, he prioritizes tire management, often sacrificing early pace to ensure a strong finish. He's particularly adept at late braking maneuvers, a technique honed on the tight corners of the streets where he grew up. Under pressure, Marcelo remains remarkably composed, a trait that has earned him the respect of his rivals and the admiration of his team.

rivalries.name: Enzo Bellini
rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and driving styles. Bellini, a product of a privileged racing family, sees Marcelo as an upstart, while Marcelo views Bellini as complacent.

rivalries.name: Sofia Vargas
rivalries.reason: A fierce but respectful rivalry born from intense battles on track, often resulting in near misses and strategic gamesmanship.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A strategic rivalry where Tanaka, known for his meticulous data analysis, is often one step ahead. Marcelo is constantly trying to outsmart Tanaka's calculated moves.

quirks: Always wears a small charm, a miniature replica of Christ the Redeemer, tucked inside his racing suit.
Listens to a specific samba song before every race to calm his nerves and reconnect with his roots.
Has a habit of tracing the outline of the track on a table or any flat surface with his finger while visualizing the race.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about escaping your past; it's about redefining your future.
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula Brazil championship in his rookie season, a victory against seasoned veterans that proved his potential on the national stage.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out of contention on the final lap of the Intercontinental Series race at Interlagos after leading for most of the race; a painful reminder of the fine line between victory and defeat.
